ink-faint.contrastNote: 5.04:1 vs paper (light), 8.32:1 vs paper (dark) — both clear WCAG AA 4.5:1 for text, verified 2026-09-04.

sealing-wax.contrastNote: 4.74:1 vs paper / 5.92:1 vs panel (light), 5.83:1 vs paper / 5.00:1 vs panel (dark) — brightened from the redesign's first-pass #a8391f at the user's explicit request for more accent presence; verified 2026-09-04.

accent-tint.purpose: Light background fill behind branch tags, added in the same pass as the brighter accent so tags read as distinct marks instead of a thin outline that's easy to miss.

display.purpose: Every classification name and heading, always uppercase — the site brand, Explore row names, detail panel name, quiz question/result. The brand itself runs large (clamp(3.4rem, 11vw, 7rem)) so it reads as the first viewport's actual headline.

title.purpose: Section intros and the same oversized-uppercase treatment as display, at a slightly narrower size range for secondary headings.

body.purpose: Running prose — descriptions, taglines, hints — plus the rotated tab labels.

mono.purpose: Anything measured: indices, era dates, diagnostic labels, branch tags, footer credits, timeline marks. A number set in this face reads as data, not prose.

extensions.shadowNote: This system uses no box-shadow anywhere — see DESIGN.md's 'The Line, Not Light Rule'. Separation between surfaces comes from a 1px border (rule-solid for flush content, ink for floating panels) or a paper/panel tone shift, never blur.

motion.name: ease-cut
motion.purpose: Every state change (view fade-in, tooltip/popover appearance, row hover) steps rather than eases — an instant two-or-three-frame cut instead of a smooth curve, matching the system's printed/mechanical register.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Brand tagline switches from right-aligned to left-aligned and drops its max-width.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Tab row gap tightens for small phones.

components.name: Tab
components.description: Rotated vertical label riding a dashed grid rule — the header's view switcher. The active state's rule is now sealing-wax red (was ink) for a small deliberate dash of color in the header.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 2rem; height: 78px; align-items: flex-end; border-bottom: 1px solid #cfcfcf; } .ds-tab { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: flex-end; height: 100%; background: none; border: none; padding: 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tab-rule { flex: 1; width: 0; border-left: 1px dashed #606060; } .ds-tab-label { writing-mode: vertical-rl; transform: rotate(180deg); font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #606060; margin-top: 0.5rem; } .ds-tab--active .ds-tab-rule { border-left-style: solid; border-left-color: #c22400; border-left-width: 2px; } .ds-tab--active .ds-tab-label { color: #161616; font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Branch filter above the Explore list and the Compare picker. Now a solid white (panel) fill rather than transparent, so each chip reads as a distinct element against the grey paper page.
components.css: .ds-chip-row { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; } .ds-chip { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #474745; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #161616; border-radius: 0; padding: 0.4rem 0.75rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip:hover { border-color: #c22400; color: #c22400; } .ds-chip--active { background: #161616; border-color: #161616; color: #e6e6e6; }

components.name: Branch Tag
components.description: Classification-branch mark: sealing-wax text and border over a light accent-tint fill (revised from a fully transparent outline, which read as too faint).
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-block; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.65rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: #c22400; background: color-mix(in srgb, #c22400 12%, #ffffff); border: 1px solid #c22400; padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 0; }

components.name: Spec Row
components.description: Explore-list row: index, oversized display name, live specimen (set in the classification's own verified font), tagline, era, branch tag.
components.css: .ds-row { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 1.25rem; width: 100%; text-align: left; background: none; border: none; border-top: 1px solid #cfcfcf; padding: 1rem 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-row:hover { background: #ffffff; } .ds-row-index { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.68rem; color: #606060; width: 24px; flex-shrink: 0; padding-top: 0.4em; } .ds-row-main { flex: 1; } .ds-row-name { display: block; font-family: Anton, sans-serif; font-size: 2rem; text-transform: uppercase; line-height: 1; color: #161616; } .ds-row-specimen { display: block; margin-top: 0.4rem; font-family: Georgia, serif; font-size: 1.5rem; color: #474745; } .ds-row-tagline { display: block; margin-top: 0.3rem; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.82rem; color: #474745; } .ds-row-meta { flex-shrink: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-end; gap: 0.4rem; } .ds-row-era { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.68rem; color: #606060; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: The "try your own text" custom specimen field.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Type or paste a word…" />
components.css: .ds-input { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.92rem; padding: 0.6rem 0.85rem; border: 1px solid #cfcfcf; border-radius: 0; background: #ffffff; color: #161616; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #606060; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #161616; outline-offset: 1px; border-color: #606060; }

components.name: Floating Panel
components.description: The detail modal and quiz card shell — no shadow; separation from the page comes entirely from the solid ink border.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #161616; border-radius: 0; padding: 2rem; max-width: 640px; } .ds-panel-era { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; color: #606060; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-panel-name { font-family: Anton, sans-serif; font-size: 2.4rem; text-transform: uppercase; line-height: 0.95; margin-top: 0.35rem; color: #161616; }

narrative.overview:
Type Classified reads as a technical reference, not a book: a page built like a measured drawing, where a dashed rule and a leader line prove a claim instead of decorating it. This replaced an earlier 'Specimen Ledger' identity (warm parchment, a serif display face, soft ambient shadows) at the user's explicit direction, pinned to two references — a portfolio built from massive stacked client names, and the Cooper Hewitt Museum's 'Type Culture Now' poster, with its dashed vertical grid and rotated section labels — translated onto a white ground instead of the originals' black.

A follow-up pass corrected the neutrals to genuine grey (paper was still faintly warm at #efece6; now #e6e6e6), brightened and re-saturated the accent (#a8391f -> #c22400 light, #d9714a -> #ff5a33 dark), gave branch tags a light tint fill so they read clearly instead of nearly disappearing, and enlarged the brand headline substantially (clamp(2.4rem,7vw,4rem) -> clamp(3.4rem,11vw,7rem)) so it functions as the first viewport's actual headline.

Every classification name is set in a single oversized condensed grotesque, uppercase, carrying the page the way a poster's headline carries a spread. Everything measured — indices, era dates, diagnostic labels, dimension callouts — is set in a monospace, because a number in a monospace face reads as data, not prose. Corners are square throughout and nothing casts a shadow — separation between surfaces comes from a rule line or a change in tone, never blur.
keyCharacteristics: Genuinely neutral light grey ground (not a warm off-white), near-black ink, white raised panels
One condensed display face (Anton) carries every name and headline, always uppercase, at a deliberately large scale
A monospace face marks anything measured: indices, dates, dimensions, tags
Dashed rules are structural, not decorative — they mark a grid, a leader line, a boundary
Square corners everywhere; separation comes from a rule or a tone change, never a shadow
One bright accent color marks small things — tags (with a tint fill), bars, the active tab, measurement call-outs — never a large fill

rules.name: The Small Mark Rule
rules.body: Sealing Wax never fills a surface larger than a tag, a 2px border, or a bar on the timeline — a tag's light accent-tint background is a tint, not a fill, and stays inside this rule.

rules.name: The No-Warm-Neutral Rule
rules.body: No neutral in this system carries a warm cast in either direction — paper, panel, ink, and rule are all genuinely neutral grey, black, or white.

rules.name: The One Voice, One Data Rule
rules.body: Anton names things; Inter explains things; JetBrains Mono measures things. No role ever borrows another's job.

rules.name: The Line, Not Light Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow appears anywhere in this system. A surface separates from the page behind it with a border or a tone change; if neither reads clearly enough, the surface's content or size is wrong, not its shadow.

dos: Do set every classification name and heading in Anton, uppercase, at large scale.
Do set anything measured (an index, a date, a diagnostic, a dimension) in JetBrains Mono.
Do separate every surface with a border or a tone shift, never a shadow.
Do keep Sealing Wax to tags (with a tint fill), bars, and measurement marks — bright, but still small.
donts: Don't reintroduce a shadow anywhere, however soft.
Don't round a corner. border-radius: 0 is absolute, no exceptions — including SVG geometry.
Don't bring back a warm-toned neutral.

Don't ship a font whose classification lineage is wrong for the sake of a better-looking specimen — the live Aa Gg Qy specimens still render in each classification's own verified typeface beneath the new Anton display name, not replaced by it.
